memory_state_inventory.call_order: Call map lists all 22 original call sites in ascending code order; per-tile and clip-dependent repetition is stated at each call.

constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic: MSC target ABI: int/unsigned are 16-bit, long is 32-bit; mode selectors 1/2/3; bpp 2/6/2; rowbytes 0x80/0x48/0x20; div 2/2/8; clip sentinel 500.
Coordinate / and % are signed 16-bit IDIV semantics, truncating toward zero; compiler-visible widths and source types agree on the valid display domain.

wt/ht, wpix, skip, tile index and ht*wt*rowbytes are computed with 16-bit machine products/low words. n is unsigned 16-bit for _fmemset; `(long)(int)(n + 4)` forces wrapped 16-bit sum -> signed int16 -> sign-extended long32, matching original CWD.

The original `cdq` alias at 0x4E0D is an unprefixed 16-bit CWD in CS_MODE_16; corrected candidate allocation site at 0x4E04 likewise executes CWD. The decoder mnemonic alone is not treated as width proof; default operand size and absence of 0x66 were checked.

Far queue arrays use 4-byte handles/message pointers and 4-byte Pnt entries; plane elements and cache elements are 2 bytes. `pic[4]`/`pic[5]` read words at byte offsets +8/+10; source pixels are pic+8; output header uses words at bufp+0/+2 and pixel data/memset begins at bufp+4.
Per-tile idx is signed `ty*40 + balTileRect.left`; only `[0,1200)` is written in the 2-byte fd_50F6_15C4 cache. dst advances by signed skip per row and bpp per tile; callback stride is wpix.
The mode switch has fallthrough from case 2 into case 1, no indirect switch jump, and no default initializer for div; valid LoadTiles paths assign 1/2/3 for supported graphics-mode tags.

static_axes.axis: whole Balloon resource dimensions and allocation domain
static_axes.evidence: MakeBalloon copies through `_fstrcpy` into a 300-byte allocation without an enforced length check, measures each line from live font metrics, has a 10-line scan break but no width/height clamp, then stores width/height in signed 16-bit header fields. DrawBalloons trusts those fields and does not bound wt, ht, n, or allocator size. Thus no code-enforced bound excludes the high-bit allocation-sum domain; the corrected cast handles every resulting 16-bit sum.

Original allocation site is CWD under 16-bit operand size; corrected MSC 6.00AX whole-module output uses the matching CWD sequence; executed n=0x7ffc expression probe returns FFFF:8000, while the unsigned control returns 0000:8000. Width-boundary full-function capture also matches at sum 7ffc and across the 8000 sign boundary.

Original helpers execute through PreparedPair except registered suite callbacks. The width boundary hook stops at the real allocator entry before its first instruction, with no allocator result stub. The archived finite suite observes logical callbacks and projected pointed bytes, not final physical framebuffer/backend tile state.

review_notes: Original disassembly came from `python tools/context.py DrawBalloons` with no `--raw`; the worker's original-context.txt is pinned. No raw original byte capsule is stored.

Current registered-source receipt keeps the actual 0x4E0D width mismatch explicit and UNRESOLVED. The separate corrected-source receipt is a candidate for root review only; it has not changed evidence/behavior/manifest.json, any v1 packet, canonical src/, layout/manifest.json or promotion history.

Supported fd_50F6_1102 values are 1/2/3 as established by `LoadTiles` for enumerated g_5A97 graphics tags. Unrecognized graphics tags leave the mode global unchanged; invalid direct entry state is not claimed as a normal game path.

MakeBalloon has no enforced message-length, width, or height limit. Its 300-byte scratch allocation and 10-line scan do not statically bound every source string or font metric; therefore no maximum `n` is asserted. The corrected cast matches the original for every 16-bit wrapped allocation sum, while large-buffer service behavior itself is not exercised by the finite render suite.

The archived suite expects a sibling deps/ folder that is not present in its immutable run snapshot. Worker copies of suite.py, behavior_ledger.py and memory.py are byte-identical to their pinned immutable sources; the run evidence records their hashes. No frozen packet was repaired or rewritten.

The separate stack-alias probe executes normal queue counts 1..6 with the first visible entry at each index 0..5, comparing full original/candidate state and call arguments. Its matrix records that i=1 deliberately aliases live pos in both builds and i=2 aliases shown in both; i=3/i=4 have differing compiler homes, but every affected home is overwritten before use. The allocation sign-boundary positive/negative controls also run at queue count 5, visible index 4.
Candidate has no historical byte-exact claim: its compiler-generated function extent/relocation placement remains inexact. The strict static verdict is behavioral, pending independent root review.

root_review.basis: Reviewed the whole-function branch/call/state/width maps, source/evidence identities, explanations of residue and differential/negative limits. Matching observed service boundaries are composed through the actual caller ABI and same callee/slot/state; finite coverage alone is not acceptance.
root_review.note: Only allocation widening changes: signed reinterpretation of the wrapped word before long widening reproduces original CWD for every 16-bit sum. Six legal queue-index paths and explicit stack-home liveness matrix resolve the hs[1] alias concern; negative width controls detect the old unsigned extension. Old registered source remains UNRESOLVED in its separate receipt.
